# Market, company and competitor context (EXTERNAL)

Last checked 2026-09-24. Every fact below comes from a public web source. Each one gives the publisher, the title, the
publication date, the URL and the date it was retrieved. None of it is the project's data, and none of it was checked
against the project's data. The analyst labels these facts **EXTERNAL**, a fourth label next to REAL, SYNTHETIC and
METHOD.

Rules for this file:
- Only facts the fetched page itself states. A search-engine summary is not a source.
- Sales-based figures are left out on purpose: revenue, GMV/GOV/NOV, order counts, profit or margin, and market share.
  Public reports do contain them. But the project cannot measure any of them, and the analyst refuses those questions,
  so quoting company sales figures would reopen exactly the claims the project keeps closed.
- An EXTERNAL fact never confirms or contradicts a SYNTHETIC result. For example, the generator's Flipkart Minutes
  price level was planted by hand (docs/GENERATOR_v15_PARAMETERS.md). No news report makes it more or less real.

## Bhubaneswar: which platforms operate, and how many stores

A public store map lists, for Bhubaneswar: Blinkit 8 stores, Swiggy Instamart 10, Flipkart Minutes 6, BigBasket 6, and
shows Zepto as not operating in Bhubaneswar. The page says it was last verified on 2026-07-10. It says its locations
"are compiled from each platform's publicly observable store-locator information and are approximate (typically within
about 100 m)".

**Same source as the project's store master.** `data/reference/STORES*.csv` was built from this map (its `source`
column reads "QuickCommerceMap public store listings"). So the agreement below is a freshness check, not independent
validation. Re-fetched on 2026-09-24, the map still lists all 30 stores of the project's master, with the same first
name segment and PIN code for each. A few address suffixes differ, for example one Flipkart Minutes store reads
"Ghatikia Main Rd" on the site and "K-8" in the project.

Source: QuickCommerceMap, "Blinkit Stores in Bhubaneswar" and the Swiggy Instamart, Flipkart Minutes and BigBasket
Bhubaneswar pages, verified 2026-07-10. https://quickcommercemap.com/platforms/blinkit/bhubaneswar . Retrieved 2026-09-24.

## Blinkit launch in Bhubaneswar: the date is not pinned down

Prameya News reported Blinkit launching in Bhubaneswar "from today". The article body is datelined "Jan 25", but the
page shows a publication date of 8 October 2025. This source therefore does not fix the launch date, and none is
recorded here.

Source: Prameya News, "Blinkit launches in Bhubaneswar from today with lightning-fast delivery".
https://www.prameyanews.com/blinkit-launches-in-bhubaneswar-from-today-with-lightningfast-delivery . Retrieved 2026-09-24.

## Blinkit had 2,443 stores at the end of Q1 FY27

On Eternal's Q1 FY27 earnings call, Blinkit's store count was 2,443 at the end of the quarter, after adding 200 net new
stores. Management said it was "upgrading many of its existing stores and moving to a larger store size, as well as
opening larger new dark stores".

Source: MediaNama, "7 key takeaways from Eternal Q1 FY27 earnings call", published 2026-07-24.
https://www.medianama.com/2026/07/223-takeaways-eternal-q1-fy27-earnings-call/ . Retrieved 2026-09-24.

## Eternal called Q1 FY27 the peak of discounting competition

On the same call, management said "Q1 FY27 was the peak of competitive intensity that we have seen to date" and "We
don't think this level of discounting is sustainable. We don't expect this to continue beyond the near future."
Context: Q1 FY27 is April to June 2026. The project's REAL Blinkit snapshot is from 2026-07-10, just after it. One
snapshot cannot show a discounting trend, so the project can neither confirm nor refute this.

Source: MediaNama, "7 key takeaways from Eternal Q1 FY27 earnings call", published 2026-07-24.
https://www.medianama.com/2026/07/223-takeaways-eternal-q1-fy27-earnings-call/ . Retrieved 2026-09-24.

## Blinkit moved to an inventory-led model on 1 September 2025

Blinkit formally switched from a marketplace model to an inventory-led model starting September 1, 2025. Earlier that
year Eternal restructured to become an Indian-owned and controlled company (IOCC) by capping foreign ownership at
49.5%. That lets Blinkit "legally hold inventory and operate as a retailer without violating Press Note 2 (2018) under
India's FDI rules".

Source: MediaNama, "Blinkit to Fully Shift to Inventory-Led Model by Sept 2025", published 2025-07-18.
https://www.medianama.com/2025/07/223-blinkit-inventory-model-shift-2025-means-for-sellers/ . Retrieved 2026-09-24.

## Blinkit removed the 10-minute delivery promise from its branding in January 2026

On 2026-01-13, All India Radio News reported that, after government intervention, a meeting was held with leading
platforms including Blinkit, Zepto, Zomato and Swiggy. It said Blinkit "has already acted on the directive and removed
the 10-minute delivery promise from its branding". The stated aim was "ensuring greater safety, security and improved
working conditions for gig workers".

Source: All India Radio News (newsonair.gov.in), news report published 2026-01-13 (no title was captured; the URL
slug reads "delivery aggregators agree to drop 10-minute delivery deadline after government intervention sources").
https://www.newsonair.gov.in/delivery-aggregators-agree-to-drop-10-minute-delivery-deadline-after-government-intervention-sources .
Retrieved 2026-09-24.

## Swiggy Instamart had 1,171 dark stores in 131 cities after Q1 FY27

In its Q1 FY27 results, Swiggy added 28 dark stores, taking Instamart's total to 1,171 stores across 131 cities and over
4.9 million square feet.

Source: Goodreturns, report on Swiggy's Q1 FY27 results, published 2026-07-30. (The headline reports financial
figures, which this file does not use; only the store figures are taken.)
https://www.goodreturns.in/amphtml/news/swiggy-q1-results-revenue-jumps-37-net-loss-narrows-to-rs-791-crore-as-instamart-continues-strong-1525305.html .
Retrieved 2026-09-24.

## Flipkart Minutes launched in August 2024 and passed Instamart in top-10-city dark stores

Flipkart Minutes launched in August 2024. According to CLSA, as of August 2026 it had 627 dark stores across India's top
10 cities against Swiggy Instamart's 615, and "has moved ahead of Instamart in pincode coverage across these markets".

Source: Storyboard18, "Flipkart Minutes races past Instamart in dark stores, two years into quick commerce: CLSA",
published 2026-08-26.
https://www.storyboard18.com/amp/digital/flipkart-minutes-overtakes-swiggy-instamart-in-dark-stores-ws-l-108835.htm .
Retrieved 2026-09-24.

## Flipkart Minutes had 1,000 micro-fulfilment centres in 130 cities

Flipkart Minutes had 1,000 micro-fulfilment centres covering 130 cities and more than 8,000 pin codes. A UBS report
projects about 1,000 more by mid-2027 or Big Billion Days 2027, to around 2,000. The article says that in non-metro
markets "customers are more willing to accept delivery times of 25-30 minutes".

Source: Inc42, "Flipkart Minutes Could Add 1,000 Dark Stores By Mid-2027: UBS", published 2026-09-04.
https://inc42.com/buzz/flipkart-minutes-could-add-1000-dark-stores-by-mid-2027-ubs/ . Retrieved 2026-09-24.

## BigBasket is majority-owned by Tata Digital

BigBasket was founded in December 2011. In May 2021, Tata Group subsidiary Tata Digital acquired a 64% majority stake.
BB Now is BigBasket's quick-delivery division. The source gives no store count or delivery promise for BB Now, so none
is recorded here.

Source: Wikipedia, "BigBasket". https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BigBasket . Retrieved 2026-09-24. (An encyclopedia entry
is a weaker source than a filing or a news report.)

## Distributors asked the competition regulator to look at deep discounting

The All India Consumer Products Distribution Federation (AICPDF) complained to the Competition Commission of India
(CCI) about below-cost sales and deep discounting by Blinkit, Swiggy Instamart and Zomato, warning that such tactics
are "significantly harming small retailers and traditional kirana stores". A formal petition was filed in March 2025.
As of the article, the CCI had not launched a formal investigation. It had asked the complainant for additional
evidence before deciding whether to open an inquiry.

Source: MediaNama, "Predatory Pricing in Quick Commerce CCI Under Scrutiny", published 2025-08-14.
https://www.medianama.com/2025/08/223-india-quick-commerce-predatory-pricing-cci/ . Retrieved 2026-09-24.
